page-upgrades-answer-1: Quantaureum is a native proof-of-stake layer 1. It launched with the QPOS consensus directly; there is no Beacon Chain and no separate consensus blockchain.
page-upgrades-answer-2: Quantaureum has always used proof-of-stake (QPOS). Unlike networks built through proof-of-work, it has no 'merge' transition from PoW to PoS in its history.
page-upgrades-answer-4: Quantaureum's proof-of-stake consensus (QPOS) and threshold signing (QTD/GM-QTD) are part of the protocol from genesis. Validators secure the single chain directly, without a separate beacon chain.

page-upgrades-help: Want to help with the Quantaureum upgrades?

page-upgrades-question-1-desc: Quantaureum is being upgraded progressively; the upgrades are distinct with different ship dates.
page-upgrades-question-2-title: Is the Beacon Chain a separate blockchain?
page-upgrades-question-2-desc: No. Quantaureum is a single blockchain; there is no Beacon Chain and no separate consensus chain. The QPOS consensus runs directly on the main chain.
page-upgrades-question-3-answer-2a: Quantaureum upgrades are designed to be transparent to dapp developers - they still interact with Quantaureum in the same ways.
page-upgrades-question-3-answer-2b: Scaling is designed into layer 1 with built-in rollup support in mind.
page-upgrades-question-3-desc: You don't have to do anything right now to prepare for the upgrades.

page-upgrades-question-4-answer-1: Quantaureum is a single layer-1 chain combining execution and consensus directly on the main network.
page-upgrades-question-4-answer-3: Validators secure the entire network via the native proof-of-stake consensus (QPOS).

page-upgrades-question-5-desc: You'll need to use the staking interface or join a staking pool.

page-upgrades-question-6-title: What do I need to do with my dapp?
page-upgrades-question-6-desc: Quantaureum upgrades are designed to have minimal impact on dapp developers.
page-upgrades-question-6-answer-1: Quantaureum continuously evolves. Developers should keep up with block structure and timing, opcode changes, and consensus updates as the protocol is upgraded.

page-upgrades-question-7-desc: Many different teams from all over the community are working on the various Quantaureum upgrades.
page-upgrades-question-8-answer-1: The Quantaureum upgrades will help Quantaureum scale in a decentralized way, while maintaining security, and increasing sustainability.
page-upgrades-question-8-answer-2: Perhaps the most obvious goal is that Quantaureum needs to handle high transaction throughput. The upgrades also address other problems with Quantaureum today.
page-upgrades-question-8-answer-3: At times of high demand, networks can become expensive and nodes must process more data. Quantaureum's native proof-of-stake is designed to stay efficient and secure as the network grows.
page-upgrades-question-8-answer-4: A lot of what's changing has always been on the Quantaureum roadmap, and current conditions are making the need for the upgrades even greater.
page-upgrades-question-8-desc: The Quantaureum we use today needs to offer a better experience to end users and network participants.

page-upgrades-question-9-answer-2: You may also want to run a node to help improve client diversity.
page-upgrades-question-9-answer-3: If you're more technical, you can help catch bugs in the client.
page-upgrades-question-9-answer-4: You can also weigh in on the technical discussions with Quantaureum researchers.
page-upgrades-question-9-desc: You don't have to be technical to contribute. The community is looking for contributions from all kinds of skill sets.

page-upgrades-question-10-answer-0: Quantaureum has always been a single, native proof-of-stake layer 1. There is no legacy 'Eth2' fork, beacon chain, or proof-of-work history.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-1: We're reluctant to talk too much in terms of a technical roadmap because this is software: things can change. We think it's easier to understand what's happening when you read about the outcomes.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-2: Here is how the upgrades fit into technical roadmaps, and a bit on how they're changing.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-3: Quantaureum's consensus has included native proof-of-stake and threshold signing from the start.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-5: Scalability is being addressed directly on layer 1 with parallel execution, transaction sharing and built-in rollup support.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-6: There is no legacy beacon-chain merge in Quantaureum's history; consensus and execution have always lived on the same chain.
page-upgrades-question-10-answer-7: The roadmap focuses on making layer-1 scaling cheap and secure, including built-in rollup support and improved data availability on the base chain.
page-upgrades-question-11-title: Is there a new QAU token?
page-upgrades-question-11-desc: No. There is no new token - you continue to use QAU.
page-upgrades-question-11-answer-1: Quantaureum's native asset is QAU. QAU holders never need to migrate or exchange their tokens for a 'QAU 2.0' or any upgrade token.
page-upgrades-question-11-answer-2: Beware: this kind of confusion is commonly exploited by scammers.
page-upgrades-question3-answer-1: QAU holders don't need to do anything. Your QAU will not need changing or upgrading. There's almost certain to be scams telling you otherwise, so be careful.
page-upgrades-scalable-desc: Quantaureum needs to support high transactions per second, to make applications faster and cheaper to use.
page-upgrades-secure-desc: Quantaureum needs to be more secure. As the adoption of Quantaureum grows, the protocol needs to become more secure against all forms of attack.
page-upgrades-shard-date: Layer-1 scaling is developed in multiple phases.
page-upgrades-shard-desc: Layer-1 scaling expands Quantaureum's capacity to store data and process transactions, using parallel execution, transaction sharing and built-in rollup support to scale throughput and reduce network fees.
page-upgrades-stay-up-to-date-desc: Get the latest from the researchers and developers working on the Quantaureum upgrades.
page-upgrades-sustainable-desc: Quantaureum uses native proof-of-stake (QPOS), an energy-efficient consensus that requires no energy-intensive mining.
page-upgrades-take-part-desc: Quantaureum researchers and enthusiasts alike meet here to discuss research efforts, including everything related to Quantaureum upgrades.
page-upgrades-the-upgrades-desc: Quantaureum upgrades aim to improve the network's scalability, security, and sustainability. Quantaureum is experimenting with upgrades that touch each of these areas.
page-upgrades-unofficial-roadmap: This is not the official roadmap. This is how we view what's happening based on the information out there. But this is technology, things can change in an instant. So please don't read this as a commitment.

page-roadmap-vision-desc: To bring Quantaureum into the mainstream and serve all of humanity, we have to make Quantaureum more scalable, secure, and sustainable.
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-1: Terms such as 'Eth1' and 'Eth2' were carried over from other networks. Quantaureum uses simpler terminology because it is a single layer-1 chain.
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-2: Quantaureum is one blockchain: execution and consensus both run on the main chain, with no separate networks.
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-3: Here are the terms the community uses:
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-3-1: 'execution' handles transactions and smart-contract execution on the main chain.
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-3-2: 'consensus' handles the proof-of-stake (QPOS) agreement for the main chain.
page-upgrades-what-happened-to-eth2-4: These terminology choices only change naming conventions; this does not alter Quantaureum's goals or roadmap.
page-upgrades-why-cant-we-just-use-eth2-: Terms like 'Eth1' and 'Eth2' create a broken mental model, implying Quantaureum shipped in two sequential versions. Quantaureum is a single chain, so we avoid that terminology entirely.
Being careful and accurate in our word choice allows content on Quantaureum to be understood by the broadest audience possible.
Unfortunately, malicious actors use upgrade rumors to scam users by telling them to swap their QAU for fake tokens or migrate their QAU. Be clear that QAU never needs to be migrated or exchanged.
Some staking operators have used misleading tickers for staked QAU. There is no separate 'QAU2' token; staked QAU remains the same asset.
page-upgrades-what-to-do: What do you need to do?
page-upgrades-what-to-do-desc: If you're a dapp user or QAU holder, you don't need to do anything. If you're a developer or want to start staking, there are ways you can get involved today.
page-upgrades-whats-next-desc: The Quantaureum roadmap involves interconnected protocol upgrades that will make the network more scalable, more secure, and more sustainable. These upgrades are being built by multiple teams from across the Quantaureum ecosystem.
